the shear strength of slender GFRPC beams without shear reinforcement decreases with effective depth, due to size effect.

the LDPM can be used to simulate the shear response of GFRP RC beam specimens, and that the shear compression fracture is the dominant shear resisting mechanism in the size range investigated in this study.

the size effect in GFRP RC beam shear response is primarily governed by the shear compression fracture (i.e. crushing) of concrete in the compression zone, and that the size effect can be quantitatively explained by the size dependence of the compressive strength of concrete.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing and calibrating a meso scale computational model of concrete that is able to capture shear size effect in RC beams.
understanding the size effect on shear strength of GFRP reinforced concrete beams.

the development of advanced computational models for simulating the response of GFRP reinforced concrete beams with different sizes and shear spans, and the application of these models to gain new insight on shear strength mechanisms and size effect.

the LDPM based computational simulations provide a reliable platform for understanding the underlying mechanics that govern size effect in GFRP RC beam shear response.
size dependent shear response of GFRP RC without shear reinforcement is governed by the aggregate interlocking mechanism.
the size dependent shear response of slender RC beams without stirr-ups is governed by a combination of aggregate interlocking and fracture mechanisms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the LDPM can provide accurate predictions of strength, failure modes and load deflection curves of GFRP RC members, even in the absence of reliable experimental data on the material.
the LDPM based numerical modeling and simulation approach can be used to realistically simulate size dependent shear response of GFRP reinforced concrete beams.
a meso scale LDPM model can be used to realistically predict the strength, failure mode, and load deflection responses of slender GFRPs RC beams without shear reinforcement.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a calibrated LDPM based computational model can be used as a tool to investigate the underlying mechanics of the size effect of the shear response of slender concrete beams.
the LDPM can be used as a practical and accurate computational tool to investigate the size dependent response of RC structures.
